newsitem.title: USA: Sprint sees Q2 EPS meeting expectations.
newsitem.headline: Sprint sees Q2 EPS meeting expectations.

text.p: Sprint Corp said Monday its second quarter earnings will be in line with consensus Wall Street estimates for the period.
The most recent First Call consensus earnings per share estimate is $0.63 per share versus $0.73 in 1996.
The company will release its second quarter results on Thursday, it said.

"Over the past few days investor concerns over the costs associated with entry by long distance carriers into the local telephone markets has come to the forefront," said chairman and chief executive officer William Esrey in a press release.
"At Sprint, we are aggressively, but prudently, preparing to expand competitive local service into select major markets," he said.

Esrey's comments followed a harsh reaction on Wall Street last week to news that MCI Communications Corp would incur about twice the losses it originally anticipated as a result of its effort to enter the local phone market.

MCI shares fell $7.125 Friday to $35.25 in heavy trading on Nasdaq following its announcement Thursday that its losses would exceed $800 million for the year and 1998 losses would be even greater. MCI shares recovered some of their lost ground Monday, rising 2-3/16 from an opening price of 35 to 37-3/16 by mid-afternoon.
Sprint shares were up 3/4 to 50-1/8 in composite trading on the New York Stock Exchange Monday afternoon.
Esrey said unlike MCI, Sprint's efforts to get into the local market does not involve a heavy up-front capital investment in local facilities.
Sprint's alternative to the MCI approach calls for the resale of existing local network services and the purchase of bundled network elements, Esrey said.
"We believe the approach we are taking is more cost effective and has considerably less investment risk than the strategy being executed by some of our major competitors," Esrey said.
Esrey said Sprint's other advantage is it is already operating local systems in 19 states through more than seven million access lines.

"With our existing local switch platforms, Sprint PCS assets and our nationwide long distance network, we have an array of options at our disposal to establish local infrastructure and market presence," he said.
